final.label: typo-or-wording-in-added-text

skill_entry.name: 14. Spelling, wrong names and over-wide lines in added comments, strings and Markdown
skill_entry.trigger: The diff adds a prose line (a re-indented line counts as added): a `//`, `/* */` or ` * ` comment or a string literal in a C++ file under h/, src/, t/ or doc/, or a line of a .md file that lies outside a fenced code block (fence parity taken from the full file at HEAD). Shell, CMake and Python files, unchanged context lines, commit messages and the PR body are outside the trigger. Mechanical form: step 1 of the procedure (prose.py over `git diff BASE HEAD`).
skill_entry.procedure: 1. Extract added prose lines with HEAD line numbers. 2. Build the allow list: every word at BASE in h/ src/ t/ (identifiers split at underscores; comment and string words included), identifiers on code lines at HEAD in the touched C++ files, and file basenames at HEAD. 3. Spell-check with pyspellchecker; drop plurals, affix forms and 4-letter prefixes of code words; a word on two or more added lines is author vocabulary; read each one-off hit with no correction (run-together words). 4. Re-check allowed words that have zero code hits at HEAD (main's own comment typos). 5. Identifier-shaped tokens in comments and .md text: whole-tree count at most 1 and a one-letter-edit neighbour with two or more code hits. 6. Added .md heading case against siblings. 7. Added .md line wider than 1.25 times the widest unchanged line of its hunk.
skill_entry.question: Does this added line hold a word that neither the dictionary nor the code at BASE or HEAD knows, or a name one letter away from a real symbol, or is it a Markdown line wider than 1.25 times every unchanged line of its hunk?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: Unchanged context lines. Commit subjects and the PR body ('compelted', 'ifed', 'enqueueiung' drew no comment). Code tokens in prose that resolve, including wrong-cased ones (Prepare_hardware_attn_job, 2233 doc:53). A lowercase sentence start alone: '// in the new APi' and '// first pass will only take' at 2788a76c36:src/pos/worker.cpp:804-805 drew no comment while :791 and :809 did; '## performing attention on Hardware' at doc:1 was not flagged. Width in a new .md file, table rows, fenced code, URLs, pre-existing long lines. Grammar of a sentence that parses (2828677364 is a question). Technical claims of a doc. Fenced and backticked text. Typos in silently approved PRs (eahc, comamnds 1707; postion, tokoen 2135; actiosn 2766) are reported as nits by design; their number never changes the verdict.
skill_entry.finding_shape: A suggestion block with the corrected line and nothing else: "```suggestion\n<the one added line, corrected>\n```"; for a wrong name the same block with the symbol that exists; a repeated-word slip found by reading (2915260657 'of that of length') gets the same block, never a style remark. Over-wide Markdown line: "hmmm... our formatter didn't catch this extra-long line? Maybe it doesn't process MD docs." and on the next occurrence "same here". After a push that leaves a suggestion unapplied: "looks like this still needs fixed" (that re-check belongs to the pr-body-and-branch-state step; check 14 re-runs steps 1-7 at the new head and hands the unresolved threads over).
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: nit, unstated: 16 of 19 comments are a bare suggestion block with no severity word and no prose, and 2828679550 adds one line of praise after its block; of the two width comments one is a question about the tool (3778051701) and the other is the two-word statement 'same here' (3778058064). Never blocking: PR 2766 was approved the next day with 'Approved, assuming you'll follow up on the remaining minor comments' (review 4373886636) and PR 2499 got the suggestion and the APPROVED review in the same minute (3125494616, 4156364038).
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk only for spelling, run-together words and sentence case; hunk plus the allow list (git grep at BASE and at HEAD over h/ src/ t/, basenames from ls-tree) for the lexicon; whole-tree `git grep -c -i -w` at HEAD for identifier-shaped tokens and the HEAD identifier set for neighbours; full .md file at HEAD for fence parity and heading case; the hunk's unchanged lines for Markdown width; GNUmakefile, lefthook.yml and .github at HEAD for the 'no formatter guards it' clause, read only when step 7 fires. No callers, no CI run, no runtime.

final.widen_delta: New check 14 appended after check 13 under a new heading "Checks on added text". SKILL.md edits that follow from it: (a) "The thirteen questions" becomes fourteen with "14. Added prose line: does it hold a word neither the dictionary nor the code knows, a name one letter away from a real symbol, or a Markdown line wider than 1.25 times every unchanged line of its hunk?"; (b) the bullet "He does not comment on formatting, brace style, benchmark method, the C++ guide, or kernel arithmetic line by line" gets the exception "except an over-wide Markdown line that no formatter guards, asked as a question about the tool (3778051701)"; (c) "How Wade words a finding" gets the suggestion-block form: for a one-line text fix the whole comment is a ```suggestion block with the corrected line and no prose, one comment per line, each posted as its own COMMENTED review, repeats answered with "same here"; (d) the description line adds "misspellings, wrong symbol names and over-wide Markdown lines in added comments, strings and docs"; (e) "Report the result" adds that check 14 findings are nits that never hold approval, that every hit is reported (a widening past Wade's sampling), and that member 2915260657 (a repeated word) is reached only by reading, not by the scripts; (f) "Words used here" BASE line becomes "BASE: for an open PR `git merge-base HEAD origin/<base.ref>`; for a merged PR the PR's base sha (`gh api repos/<org>/<repo>/pulls/N --jq .base.sha`), which is the first parent of the merge commit", since merge-base against origin/main is wrong for a PR on hwattention_sync. procedures.md: the common setup's BASE line gets the same replacement; the section above is added with the On PR 2233 / 2011 / 2499 / 2766 / 3386 / silent-PR lines; the title "Procedures for the thirteen checks" becomes fourteen. Boundary notes: check 14 owns a letter-edit wrong name, comment-contradicts-adjacent-code owns a real-but-wrong symbol (3307483528); the unapplied-suggestion re-check after a push (3002050036) belongs to pr-body-and-branch-state.

final.precedent_note: n = 19 comments over 8 PRs (positron-ai/tron 2011, 2078, 2148, 2233, 2499, 2766, 2903, 3386), 2026-02-10 to 2026-08-13. No member is pasted assistant text: 17 are bare or near-bare suggestion blocks and 2 are his own short width remarks; a search of the 19 bodies for 'Claude', 'assistant', 'GPT', 'Copilot' and 'had this to say' finds nothing. Wade's only reply inside a member thread is 3002050036 (a self reply). The item file lists codex_bullets as an empty array, so no C-id was adopted or rejected.
changes_made: Lexicon (refuters disagreed): kept the full BASE word list (comment and string words included) and added the PR's own code identifiers at HEAD and file basenames (precision F1), plus an EXCUSED pass (executability F3) instead of the facts lens's code-only BASE lexicon (F7). Reason: a code-only lexicon re-admits jargon (precision: 13 hits on PR 2875; executability: readback x7, timestamps x2, doneness on PR 2011) while the EXCUSED pass recovers main's comment-only typos. Measured on this run: eahc (PR 1722), comamnds (PR 1707) and anomoly (PR 2011) surface through step 4; nshards, prepwork, prepworker, dlen, didx, ptrs no longer fire.

Step 4 counts code hits at HEAD, not at BASE (my change on top of executability F4): a PR-introduced identifier (prepwork, prepworker) then has code hits and is excused, while a word that exists only in comments or strings (anomoly, flgiht, eahc, comamnds) gets zero. The draft's step 4 was unreachable (precision, facts P7, executability all agree) and its comment-only filter kept spdlog strings (executability).

Step 3 regex keeps a word whose only capital is the first letter and lower-cases it (facts F6): 'Thsi' at worker.cpp:803 (member 2983065535) is now reported; the draft never reported it. PR 2233 now gives 7 BAD lines, not the draft's 'exactly six' or the refuters' seven-with-nshards.

Step 3 adds plural, affix (un/de/re/non/sub/pre, -s/-es/-ed/-ize/-ized/-ation/-ization) and 4-letter code-prefix rules (precision F3) and a recurrence rule; the recurrence rule is widened from no-correction hits to every hit on two or more added lines (my change): PR 3386 drops from 56 BAD lines (tctl x25, tdie, acpi, zenpower, tpmi, tccd, muxer, ftrace) to 5 one-offs; the precision lens verified that none of the 22 known Wade typos recurs.

Step 1 restricted to C++ files under h/ src/ t/ doc/ and .md files; shell, CMake and Python files are outside the trigger; the `#` comment marker is dropped (executability F9, precision F2). PR 1727 goes from 46 prose lines to 16 and from 3 hits to 0.

Fence handling computes parity from the full file at HEAD, not from the hunk (my fix of precision F2 as written): with hunk-local toggling the README.perfetto.md:273 width finding of PR 3386 was lost; with full-file parity both Wade width findings reproduce and the fenced README.perfetto.md:33-34 lines of PR 1727 drop out.

Step 5 (refuters disagreed): kept a letter-edit rule (one missing, extra, substituted or transposed letter; precision F5, facts F8) with two extra conditions, the neighbour must have two or more code occurrences and the same name in another case convention does not count; rejected the executability lens's fragment-based neighbour search because it maps xfer_wait to wait_for_xfer_blocks and consumed_head_index to last_consumed_head_index (Wade posted neither) and cannot find LOG_TOKEN_TIMES from LOG_TOKEN_TIMS ('tims' is not a fragment of it). Measured: LOG_TOKEN_TIMS is the only FIND across the 9 PRs run; string literals are excluded from step 5 (executability F5).

BASE recipe replaced (executability F1) with my refinement: open PR = merge-base against origin/<base.ref> (GitHub's base.sha moves with the branch), merged PR = the PR's base sha = first parent of the merge commit; verified base.sha equals the refuters' BASE for 2011, 2233, 1707, 1722, 2135, 2766.

Severity sentence corrected to 16 bare blocks plus 2828679550 with praise, and 3778058064 as a statement (facts F1); quote what_it_shows for 3307296300 (12 reviews) and 3125494616 (LOG_TOKENT_IMES history, 3124878965 was about the #define) rewritten (facts F2, F15); 3778058064 wording adjusted.

do_not_fire rewritten: the worker.cpp:798-799 clause now cites 2788a76c36:804-805 (facts F3); the sampling list drops thrreaded and fundamanetal, which the author fixed with no comment (facts F4); the 'tokoen at :34' sentence replaced by the silent-PR typo list with 2135 as the PR that added tokoen and postion (precision); the 558c1f1f6 'he approved' claim replaced by the 18:27Z/18:31Z timing (facts F11).

Code facts corrected: driver.cpp lines 440-442 at d4d6524dd5 and :771 / :664 applied lines (facts F5); doc line widths 11 to 344 with seven lines of 118 or more (F9); README.perfetto.md 26 lines over 100 characters at lines 3, 24, 30, 57, 61, 63 (F10); '23 noise lines' replaced by '48 without the lexicon against 7 with it' (F14); tooling counts restated on the named list (F13).
Member 2915260657 (repeated word 'of that of') named as not reached by the scripts; step 8 adds a one-pass read of added comment sentences and the finding keeps the suggestion-block form (facts F12).
Step 8's post-push 'looks like this still needs fixed' re-check handed to pr-body-and-branch-state, and the boundary with comment-contradicts-adjacent-code stated (precision).

Step 7 reads GNUmakefile and lefthook.yml only when a width line is reported, quoting the HEAD's own format target (executability F6); step 6 skips fenced lines so shell comments inside code blocks are not read as headings (my addition after the 3386 heading list showed '# then: perfetto/tronperf' from a fence).
Tooling sentence: pyspellchecker through uv is served from the cache after the first run; codespell fallback named with what it misses (executability F8, facts F13).
residual_risks: Wade samples; this check reports every hit (9 silent-PR typos across 1707, 1722, 2135, 2766, 2499 would each become a nit). The entry labels them nits and says their number never changes the verdict, but an author may still see more typo comments than Wade would post.

One-off no-correction hits and one-off dictionary gaps are read by hand: on PR 3386 that is 5 reads (cpulist, interruptible, cpuinfo, dtpm, cpuidle) and on PR 1722 one (kcache); on PR 2011 two step-4 reads (anomoly, doneness). The procedure says what to drop, but the decision is the agent's.

Review-time heads 4ef7ac4371, cef0fb5b64 (PR 2766), 4b7d03f71c, d634595662 (PR 2233), a42fb63fd6, ab5c1c2919 (PR 2499) are not in the worktree; the flgiht case (3307465363) and the aremultiple, versin, LOG_TOKENT_IMES hunks are verified from the digest and gh api contents only, not by running the scripts.

The width threshold (1.25 times the widest unchanged prose line of the hunk) reproduces both PR 3386 findings and fires on nothing at 558c1f1f6, on PR 2233 or on the nine silent PRs; it has not been tried on another Markdown-heavy PR with a width comment, because the corpus has none.
The step-5 letter-edit rule is tuned on one positive case (LOG_TOKEN_TIMS); a wrong name two letters away from its symbol would not fire.
The recurrence rule hides a typo the author repeats on two or more added lines (psuedochannel x2 in PR 1722 is one; Wade did not flag it either).

pyspellchecker needs network on the first `uv run --with` use; on a machine without it the check degrades to codespell (3 of the 4 PR 2011 words, no run-together words) and must say Insufficient data.

The allow-list HEAD source reads only the C++ files the diff touches; a PR identifier introduced in a file the diff does not touch cannot exist, but an identifier from a Python or shell file the PR adds is not vocabulary and would appear as a hit in a .md file that mentions it.
